# Chemist
You are the department's supply line. Nobody else can make what you make, and the line cannot hold without it.
Your loop is three steps: [bold]harvest[/bold], [bold]brew[/bold], [bold]deliver[/bold]. All three happen during the wave, not between them.
## 1. Harvest
Your satchel renders tissue from wave enemies that die near you. You do not click anything - stand where the fighting is and it fills on its own.
There is a ceiling per wave. The gauge on the left of your HUD shows how close you are; when it turns amber you have taken everything this wave will give you, and your time is better spent delivering than standing in the line.
Tissue is the base ingredient for every field potion. No tissue, no potions - which is why the loop starts at the front and not at the bench.
## 2. Brew
Brewing happens at the [bold]field kit station[/bold]. Use your satchel on it, or press Dump, and the tissue goes into its tank. The tank stays in the machine and every chemist on shift brews from it.
Put a jug in, pick a batch size (a flask, a magazine or the whole jug), and press Brew on a potion. The station measures both parts and puts the finished potion in the jug.
Every field potion is [bold]2 tissue + one reagent from the station's stock[/bold]. No sub-recipes, no heating step.
- [bold]Combat Stim[/bold] - tissue + sugar. Hits harder, swings and shoots faster, moves quicker. - [bold]Corrosive[/bold] - tissue + sulfur. Leaves caustic damage on the ground. - [bold]Solvent[/bold] - tissue + fluorine. Stops armoured and giant zombies regrowing their plating. - [bold]Weakening Agent[/bold] - tissue + mercury. Everything in the cloud takes 25% more damage from every source.
Two more, [bold]Etchant[/bold] and [bold]Coagulant Mist[/bold], need precursors the CMO unlocks on the medical research console. Print the precursor bottle at the lathe and load it into the station.
The station's Raw Dispense tab is a full chemical dispenser for anything else a doctor asks for.
## 3. Deliver
[bold]The syringe gun[/bold] shoots teammates, not zombies. It cannot hurt crew. Magazines hold 200 darts at 1u each, so a single magazine covers most of a wave - fill one at the syringe filler and carry spares.
Darts cannot overdose anyone. The gun trims each dose to whatever the target can still safely take, so you can hold fire on a wounded ally without poisoning them.
[bold]Splash flasks[/bold] are thrown and burst into a cloud. Buff clouds land on everyone inside, so throwing one into a group is worth far more than four separate darts. Anti-zombie clouds never harm crew or player structures.
## Getting paid
You earn when your work produces a result, not when you make something:
- A teammate you buffed getting a kill pays you a cut. - A doctor healing someone with a chem you produced pays you a cut.
Buffing yourself in a corner earns nothing. Being where the squad is earns everything.
## The two machines
[bold]ChemDrobe[/bold] - empty flasks, magazines and syringes. Vessels are free; contents are your job.
[bold]Field kit station[/bold] - its Package tab loads a magazine straight from the jug and fills the empty flasks you have racked on it. Bottles and pills for doctors are there too.
[bold]Syringe filler[/bold] - insert a container and a magazine and it decants one into the other on its own. Handy for a jug brewed somewhere else.
